sources.entry: git-worktree: manage multiple working trees attached to the same repository.

summary.title: git-worktree documentation
summary.one_liner: git worktree lets you check out several branches of one repository at once in separate linked working trees, and shows how to add, list, lock, move, repair, prune and remove them.
keywords: check out two branches at once
takeaways: git worktree add <path> creates a linked working tree sharing the repository, optionally creating a new branch named after the path.
Use git worktree remove for clean-up; prune handles worktrees deleted manually without removal.
git worktree lock prevents pruning for worktrees on portable or network-mounted drives.
Refs are shared across worktrees except pseudo refs like HEAD; config can be per-worktree with extensions.worktreeConfig.
The docs state multiple checkout is experimental and submodule support is incomplete; not recommended for superprojects.
summary.summary: This is the official Git reference page for the git-worktree command. It defines linked and main worktrees, describes each subcommand (add, list, lock, move, prune, remove, repair, unlock) with its options, and explains how refs, per-worktree config and the GIT_DIR/GIT_COMMON_DIR layout work. It includes list output formats, a worked emergency-fix example, and the related config variables. The page is a reference manual, so it is dense and organized by command rather than as a guided tutorial.
